text.p: Pennsylvania's legislature early Tuesday approved a plan to deregulate the state's electricity market, sending the bill to the governor.
"The bill was approved at 10:15 (EST) last night (Monday) by the Senate and by the House about 2:00 this morning," said Steve Miskin, a spokesman for Gov. Tom Ridge.

"This legislation will mean lower electric bills for working Pennsylvania families, more jobs for working Pennsylvanians, and more choices for Pennsylvania consumers," Ridge said in a prepared statement. "I will gladly sign this bill into law."
Pennsylvania becomes the fourth state to enact legislation deregulating its electricity industry, following California, New Hampshire, and Rhode Island.

The legislation seeks to give one-third of the state's consumers an opportunity to choose their electricity supplier by the end of 1998, expanding retail competition to include all consumers by January, 2001.
Electric distribution companies will continue to be the supplier of last resort to ensure universal and reliable electric service.

As part of the plan, electricity rates will be capped from Jan. 1, 1997, for nine years while transmission and distribution rates will be capped for at least four-and-a-half years and possibly as long as nine.
The caps seek to ensure that consumers who do not select a power supplier do not end up paying more for their electricity than those prices current in January, 1997.

Under the new law, the state's Public Utilities Commission can order utilities to conduct pilot competitive retail programmes from April 1, 1997, tapping for each programme 5 percent of a utility's peak load for at least a year.
The response from the main investor-owned utilities operating in the state was generally positive.

"GPU Energy certainly agrees with lawmakers that competition will be more effective than regulation at lowering prices and stimulating economic development," said Dennis Baldassari, president of GPU Energy, a unit of GPU Inc.

Other key utilities operating in Pennsylvania include Pennsylvania Power & Light Co., PECO Energy Co., DQE Inc., Ohio Edison Co., Orange and Rockland Utilities Inc., UGI Corp. and Allegheny Power System Inc.
Consumer groups also have lent support to deregulation.
"We supported the bill. It was a good compromise that will hopefully bring lower rates," said Irwin Popowsky at Pennsylvania's Consumer Advocate Office.
